summary: COM turns Nabd's outbound-only WhatsApp plumbing (messaging module, V44 outbox, V46/V47) into a governed two-way patient channel: persist-then-ack webhooks with STOP honoured in under a minute, a separate Comms Gateway (ADR-01) with one notification contract, branded senders (shared Nabd number first, clinic numbers via embedded signup in Phase 2), quality-aware throttling, send windows with quiet hours and KSA prayer times, India DLT SMS fallback, the reception shared inbox, the WhatsApp booking conversation on the Patient Access Edge, and the engagement module (recall engine, reviews, feedback, complaints, referral rewards). stories.title: Store every WhatsApp webhook delivery before acknowledging it, and drop duplicates by wamid
stories.story: As a patient I want my WhatsApp reply to reach the clinic every time so that I am not ignored, even when Meta retries or the database is slow.
stories.context: Today WhatsAppWebhookController verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC (good) but then processes statuses and templates in-line and logs-and-drops inbound messages (QA-30, MF-48). A slow insert makes Meta retry the whole batch, causing redelivery storms. The fix is persist-then-ack: verify the signature, write the raw body once to an inbound event table keyed by a dedupe key, return 200 inside 100 ms, then process asynchronously. Dedupe keys are the message wamid for inbound messages, wamid+status for status callbacks, and template id+event+timestamp for template events. The raw body can contain patient free text, so it is stored AES-GCM encrypted (existing AesGcmCipher, key version prefix) and purged after 30 days. The same story brings V46/V47 tables up to ADR-07 (FORCE RLS, array policy, WITH CHECK) because they predate it. This is built in Core's messaging module first (S4) and moves unchanged into the Comms Gateway in COM-008.
acceptance: Given a correctly signed webhook POST, when it arrives, then the raw body is persisted and 200 is returned with p95 < 100 ms at 200 rps (QA §4.4 webhook storm)
Given the same inbound message (same wamid) delivered 3 times, when all three are processed, then exactly one inbound message row exists and downstream consumers see one event
Given a webhook with a missing or wrong X-Hub-Signature-256, when it arrives, then 401 is returned, nothing is stored, and a security metric is incremented (no body logged)
Given the processor crashes mid-batch, when it restarts, then unprocessed rows are re-claimed (lease expiry) and processed exactly once by effect
Given status callbacks arrive out of order (read before delivered), when processed, then message status only moves forward (existing apply_whatsapp_status rule kept)
Given an inbound event row older than 30 days, when the purge job runs, then its encrypted raw body is deleted and only the dedupe key and outcome remain
Given any tenant table touched here (whatsapp_messages, whatsapp_templates, whatsapp_inbound_events), when the boot self-check runs, then RLS is enabled and forced

stories.title: Patient sends STOP and stops getting WhatsApp messages within one minute
stories.story: As a patient I want to reply STOP and have the clinic stop messaging me within a minute so that my choice is respected.
stories.context: STOP is dropped today, which is a Meta policy and DPDP consent breach (QA-30, R-05/R-08). The processor from COM-001 recognises opt-out keywords and quick-reply payloads in English, Hindi, Kannada, Telugu and Arabic (STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE, रोकें, بند, إيقاف, 'Stop promotions' button) and writes a consent withdrawal through the patient module's consent API (append-only consents rows, V5). Scope matters: a bare STOP withdraws the 'messaging' consent for that clinic; the 'Stop promotions' button withdraws only 'marketing'. The patient gets one confirmation (utility template, allowed after opt-out) that also says how to restart (send START). Queued messages are suppressed because WhatsAppSendHandler already checks consent at send time. When one phone is shared by a family (guardian), the withdrawal applies to every patient record under that phone in that tenant. A STOP on the shared Nabd number applies to the clinic whose conversation it replies to; with no context it applies to all clinics on the shared number.

stories.title: Meta calls fail fast and never send twice when the provider is slow
stories.story: As an engineer I want every call to Meta wrapped in timeouts, a circuit breaker and lease-fenced sends so that a provider outage never duplicates a reminder or blocks the clinic.
stories.context: Unblocks patients and reception: duplicate reminders erode trust, and a hung Meta call today can hold a DB transaction (F-10). Current gaps from docs 01 and 05: ResourceAccessException (timeout) in WhatsAppTemplateService.submitToMeta surfaces as 500 instead of 502; a failed DB insert after a successful template create leaves an orphan Meta template; WhatsAppSendHandler reads the message without FOR UPDATE and the outbox batch (20 x 10 s timeout) can outlive its 60 s lease, so two workers can send the same message (QA-29). Delivery state model gains 'cancelled' and 'expired' for COM-023.

stories.title: One notification contract every module and service uses to ask for a message
stories.story: As an engineer I want a single 'notification requested' contract with a dedupe key, priority, send window and claim-check render data so that every feature can send messages without knowing the channel and the Comms Gateway can be extracted by swapping transport only.
stories.context: Unblocks every patient-facing message (reminders, recalls, delay broadcast, secure links, owner summaries). Today WhatsAppMessageService.queueTemplate is the only producer and has no production callers (F-33). Events must carry ids only (ADR-03), yet a template needs names and times. Design: the caller's module calls NotificationPort.request(...) inside its transaction; this writes a 'notification_requests' row in Core (render params encrypted, recipient patient id, purpose, dedupe key, priority, notBefore/notAfter) and an outbox event 'comms.notification.requested.v1' with ids only. The Comms side fetches render params at send time from GET /internal/v1/notification-requests/{id} (claim check); Core answers 410 when the subject changed (appointment cancelled), which doubles as late-cancel protection. Purposes map to template keys and consent purposes (care = 'messaging', promotions = 'marketing'). Priority lanes: OTP, TRANSACTIONAL (queue, delay, secure link), REMINDER, BULK (recall, review, feedback). In S4 the consumer runs in-process; in S5 it is the Comms Gateway.
